candidates.story: OpenAI wiki incident and promised disclosure framework
candidates.reason: The existing Index Us article covers OpenAI's incident acknowledgement and future incident-disclosure framework. No checked source materially contradicts that account. The selected 12 September event is distinct: sustained third-party organisational access, verification and evaluator publication rights, not the wiki incident chronology or the promised disclosure framework itself.

The primary page is dated 10 September without an exact verified publication time and timezone; same-day AP reporting was more than 48 hours old at run start. The broad misuse theme also overlaps recent agent-security coverage.
Published by Index Us in run 20260912T021235Z. No correction or separate development was found.

decision.reason: The exact-timestamped Anthropic commitment and Altman response are fresh, consequential and distinct from prior incident-disclosure coverage. Amodei's essay specifies unusually concrete intended access and publication terms, while AP, Axios and METR provide meaningful independent context. The implementation gap and a practical procurement checklist earn a full analysis without relying on speculative catastrophe forecasts.

sources.title: X IDs
sources.locator: ID format: X uses 64-bit Snowflake IDs encoding timestamp, worker and sequence and recommends string/BigInt handling to avoid JavaScript precision loss. The two IDs were decoded as BigInt with the established Twitter Snowflake epoch 1288834974657 ms.

sources.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI industry needs to give safety measures time to catch up
sources.locator: Some of Amodei's suggestions may be more difficult to enact: ongoing outside-evaluator access, intended desks/badges/laptops and Altman's rapid commitment. Context only; not implementation evidence.

sources.title: Anthropic, OpenAI CEOs call for slowdown in AI development
sources.locator: Lines 42-71: Amodei essay, Anthropic's unilateral external-evaluator measure and Altman's statement that OpenAI would also give access. Context only; not implementation evidence.

sources.title: How independent researchers could investigate AI propensities after misalignment incidents
sources.locator: Access and resources needed and How the results should be shared: models, transcripts/reproducible environments, employee interviews, time/compute, possible training-data work, board access, public conclusions, engagement/redaction transparency and redaction summaries.

sources.title: Frontier Risk Report (February to March 2026)
sources.locator: Appendix A pilot process and AEF-1 mapping, especially table A.1 rows on technical access/resources, conflicts, methodological and editorial autonomy, publication rights, redaction authority and sensitive-information protection; METR's disclosed lack of a formal personnel conflict policy at the pilot's start.

sources.title: A shared playbook for trustworthy third party evaluations
sources.locator: How we are supporting stronger evaluations and evaluation standards: existing access to reasoning traces/intermediate artefacts for METR and Apollo, plus required disclosure of claim, tested system, budget, elicitation and validity checks.

sources.title: An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents
sources.locator: Introduction, paragraph beginning 'We have signed an agreement with METR': separate independent investigation of four cybersecurity incidents; initial eight-week term with extension by mutual agreement; wide-ranging access to transcripts beyond the incident window and employees permitted to share confidential information. The page does not identify this engagement as the permanent embedded role promised on 12 September.

claims.text: Dario Amodei announced Anthropic's embedded-evaluator commitment at 2026-09-12T14:01:10.703Z.
claims.sourceLocator: s2 public oEmbed author/text/date and status ID; s4 Snowflake timestamp documentation and retained BigInt calculation; s5-s6 same-day independent chronology.

claims.text: Sam Altman said at 2026-09-12T16:30:45.408Z that OpenAI would also use independent evaluators with employee-like access and would share more later.
claims.sourceLocator: s3 public oEmbed response and status ID; s4 Snowflake documentation/calculation; s5-s6 independent reports.

claims.text: Anthropic says the embedded evaluator's remit would include verifying safety practices and commitments, reporting incidents and assessing completed models, training pipelines and processes.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 three-step-plan item 1 and Embedded Evaluators opening.

claims.text: Anthropic intends to provide desks, badges, company laptops and access to workspaces, tools, permissions and employee conversations, mostly comparable to internal risk-assessment teams.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 access bullets; s5 physical-access reporting.

claims.text: Anthropic says access exceptions may apply for legal and contractual requirements and to protect customer and partner private information.

Anthropic says the external reviewer should control publication of key findings, while Anthropic retains narrow redaction powers for security-sensitive, legally privileged, commercially sensitive and third-party confidential information, not merely unfavourable findings.
Anthropic says a reviewer may disclose publicly when a redaction removed something important to its conclusions.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 sentence following the contract/redaction bullet.

claims.text: The checked sources do not establish that either new permanent embedded programme is operating: Anthropic says it will invite a team in the near future and does not name one for that role, while Altman supplies no team, start date, mandate, contract or report.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 future-tense invitation and absence of appointment; s3 complete response; s5-s6 report commitments rather than completed engagements; s10 documents a separate time-limited incident investigation rather than appointment to the broader role.

claims.text: METR is named only as an example of a possible permanent embedded evaluator; Anthropic's separate eight-week incident-investigation agreement does not identify METR as the appointed team for that broader role.
claims.sourceLocator: s1 uses 'such as METR' and does not identify a selected team; s10 defines a separate investigation of four cybersecurity incidents.

claims.text: Ongoing employee-like access could support longitudinal checks across training, deployment, operations, incidents and remediation that a bounded one-off model evaluation cannot establish by itself.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s1 continuous organisational remit; s7 incident-investigation access; s9 bounded-evaluation dimensions. Boundary: Index Us interpretation, not a measured effect.

claims.text: METR says a thorough independent incident investigation may require relevant-model access, transcripts or reproducible environments, employee interviews, enough time and inference budget, and sometimes training-data analysis.
METR recommends that investigation conclusions reach the board and public, with transparent engagement, access and redaction terms and a redaction summary.
claims.sourceLocator: s7 How the results should be shared.

claims.text: METR's 2026 pilot documented technical access, resources, conflicts, methodological and editorial autonomy, publication rights and redaction authority, and disclosed that it lacked a formal personnel conflict-of-interest policy at the pilot's start.
claims.sourceLocator: s8 Appendix A table A.1 and conflict disclosure.

claims.text: OpenAI says METR and Apollo have received reasoning traces and intermediate artefacts for some GPT-5-era evaluation work and argues that reports should disclose the tested claim, system, budget, elicitation and validity checks.
OpenAI's documented prior third-party evaluation access does not by itself establish the new continuous employee-like arrangement Altman promised.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: s9 selected artefact access; s3 future promise; s1 broader continuous remit. Boundary: scope comparison, not a claim that OpenAI lacks undisclosed relationships.

claims.text: A credible external-safety-review claim should disclose evaluator selection and conflicts, mandate, actual and refused access, methodological autonomy, publication and redaction rights, incident escalation and evidence that findings changed decisions.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: announced terms, METR investigation/pilot criteria and OpenAI reporting dimensions. Boundary: Index Us procurement checklist, not an industry standard.

claims.text: The selected event is distinct from Index Us's OpenAI wiki article because it concerns durable organisational access and evaluator-controlled reporting rights rather than the wiki incident chronology or OpenAI's promised incident-disclosure framework.
claims.sourceLocator: Premises: current-event scope compared with local article and run-record inspection. Boundary: editorial duplication judgement; no material correction was found.

claims.text: Anthropic says it signed a separate initial eight-week agreement, extendable by mutual agreement, for METR to independently investigate four cybersecurity incidents with wide-ranging access to transcripts beyond the incident window and employees permitted to share confidential information.
claims.sourceLocator: s10 Introduction, paragraph describing the signed METR agreement.

claims.text: METR says third-party evaluations of frontier AI have largely focused on individual models before public deployment.

artwork.concept: A cobalt external-reviewer path crosses a narrow vermilion access gate into a layered internal system, while a separate publication channel reaches an off-white public report through a visible redaction boundary. The composition makes reviewer access, independent publication and bounded redaction legible without implying a named appointment or implemented company architecture.
